description: The Spanish b/v homophone variant of the paternal surname: Nabeda for Naveda. In Spanish b and v are pronounced alike, so a scribe could write either and a genealogist must try both — this test already requires the plural-paternal Navedas, and Nabeda is the same class of variant. Matches the co-occurrence form that REQUIRES the surname as its own term (+Nabeda, present in +Nabeda +Somarriba, but NOT in the adjacent phrase +"Nabeda Somarriba"), mirroring the Naveda fixture exactly. Returns zero results: the AI transcription of these Limpias parish acts renders the name Naveda throughout, so the b spelling finds nothing and the searcher falls back to the v form. Added for issue #3592 Finding 2, where this call went unmatched and the judge auto-failed Tool Arguments on correct genealogical behaviour.

keywords.description: Full-text search query with Lucene operators. Use + to require a term, - to exclude, "..." for phrase, * for wildcard (min 3 chars). Default is OR — always use + for required terms.

name.description: Search within name fields only. Same operator syntax as keywords.

place.description: Search within place fields. Note: place matches collection metadata and can cause false positives. Prefer post-filtering.

nlQuery.description: Natural language search query or a FamilySearch tree person ID.

collectionId.description: Filter to a specific FamilySearch collection by ID.

imageGroupNumber.description: Filter to a specific digitized volume by Image Group Number.

yearFrom.description: Start of year range filter. Must be paired with yearTo.

yearTo.description: End of year range filter. Must be paired with yearFrom.

recordPlace1.description: Filter by country (or state within US/Mexico/Canada/UK).

count.description: Number of results to return. Default 5, max 100.

includeFacets.description: When true, include facet counts in the response. Default false.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the active project directory. Supply it whenever the search will be logged (the normal case): the tool then stages its raw results host-side and returns a `staged.resultsRef` handle to pass to research_log_append as stagedResultsRef, so the results are retained without re-serializing them. Only omit it for a throwaway exploratory search you are certain you will not log.
